summary: Raphael von Koeber (1848–1923) worked in philosophy and Japanology. He studied at the Moscow Conservatory, Heidelberg University, and the University of Jena, and took up a post at the University of Tokyo in 1893.

Indologist Rashmi Yadav studied at Dr. B. R. Ambedkar University, Agra, earned a diploma from Chaudhary Charan Singh University, and pursued a Ph.D. at Mahatma Jyotiba Phule Rohilkhand University. She joined Chaudhary Charan Singh University's Vedic Mathematics faculty in 2021.

Rasiklal Chhotalal Parikh (1897–1982) was an Indologist and historian who studied at Fergusson College under Bhune, R. D. Ranade, Sukhlal Sanghvi, and Muni Jinvijaya. He held posts at Gujarat Vidyapith, Puratattva, Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, and Gujarati Sahitya Parishad.

Rasmus Nyerup (1759–1829) was an Indology scholar who earned his M.A. at the University of Copenhagen. He worked at the Royal Danish Library (1784–1803) and served as Chief Librarian at the University of Copenhagen from 1796 to 1829.

Rasmus Rask (1787–1832) worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Odense Katedralskole and the University of Copenhagen, he held several Copenhagen posts, becoming professor of literary history (1825) and chair of Oriental Languages (1831).

Ratna Basu is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at the University of Bonn in 1989. She served as Professor (Special Invitee) at The Asiatic Society, attested in 2026.

Ratna Handurukande, a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies, studied under Harold Walter Bailey. She served as a lecturer at the University of Peradeniya and as a lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Ceylon, attested in 1970.
Ratna Vajra Rinpoche (born 1974) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga, whom he succeeded in 2017.

Ravi M. Gupta (born 1982) is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned degrees from Boise State and Oxford. He taught at Florida, Centre College, and William & Mary before becoming Charles Redd Chair at Utah State around 2013.

Indologist Ravi Prakash Arya studied at Panjab University. He served in Haryana's Department of Higher Education (1993–2019), directed the Indian Foundation for Vedic Science (2019–2021), and held a chair professorship at Maharshi Dayanand University (2021–2025).

Ravindra Singh Bisht (born 1944) works in archaeology and Indology. Educated at Lucknow, Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute, and Kumaun University, he served in archaeology departments in Punjab and Haryana, at the Institute of Archaeology, and as ASI Director General until 2004.

Ravindra Suryakant Kale works in Indology and computational studies. He held library posts at IOCL, Mahila Mahavidyalaya, Prof. V. B. Shah Institute, and Narmada College of Management before becoming Librarian at Shree Somnath Sanskrit University in 2014.

Ravinjay Kuckreja is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Chester (BA, 2014–2017), IE University (MA, 2017–2018), and Universitas Hindu Negeri I Gusti Bagus Sugriwa (Doctor of Religious Studies, 2020–2023).

Rawi Bhavilai (1925–2017) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and physics. He earned degrees from Chulalongkorn, Adelaide, and ANU, and served as a physics professor at Chulalongkorn University (1945–1986) and fellow of the Royal Institute of Thailand (~1986–2017).

Ray Caldwell Smith (1872–1922) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at San Francisco Theological Seminary from circa 1897 to 1900 and later held a post at the Landour Community Centre Language School.

Raymond West (1832–1912) worked in Indology and law. He studied at the University of Galway and under Martin Haug, later serving as Bombay High Court judge, Vice Chancellor of Mumbai University, and Reader in Indian Law at Cambridge.

Raymonde Linossier (1897–1930) specialized in Indology, Tibetology, and archaeology. She studied under Sylvain Lévi from circa 1920 to 1930 and was appointed as an unsalaried attachée at the Guimet Museum in 1925.

Reb Anderson (born 1943) is a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Shunryu Suzuki and Richard Baker. He succeeded Baker and served as abbot of the San Francisco Zen Center from circa 1986 to 1995.
Rebecca Hufen is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2026, she studied at the University of Hamburg as a lector for Tibetan Studies under doctoral supervisor Dorji Wangchuk.

Rebecca Redwood French is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned a J.D. from the University of Washington and a Ph.D. from Yale. She held academic posts at the University of Colorado Boulder and the University at Buffalo.
